rationales: Sr-90 is not used to diagnose thyroid goiter.
Co-60 is used mainly for radiotherapy, not thyroid diagnosis.
I-131 is taken up by the thyroid and can be used to investigate thyroid disorders.
C-14 is not the isotope used for thyroid diagnosis.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of these elements.
Chlorine is less electronegative than fluorine.
Bromine is less electronegative than chlorine and fluorine.
Iodine is less electronegative than the other listed halogens.
Non-metal atoms generally form covalent bonds by sharing electrons.
Ionic bonds usually form between a metal and a non-metal.
A coordinate covalent bond is a particular type of covalent bond, not the general expected answer here.
Metallic bonds occur between metal atoms.
The electronegativity difference between hydrogen and chlorine is approximately 1.
A difference of 2 is too large for hydrogen and chlorine.
A difference of 3 is much too large for hydrogen and chlorine.
A difference of 4 is much too large for hydrogen and chlorine.
Chlorine is a gas at room temperature.
Bromine is a liquid at room temperature.
Fluorine is a gas at room temperature.
Iodine is a solid at room temperature.
An acid solution conducts electricity because it produces ions.
Sugar solution does not produce ions and is a non-electrolyte.
NaOH solution produces ions and conducts electricity.
Ca(OH)₂ solution produces ions and conducts electricity.
Butter is a colloid in which liquid is dispersed in a solid.
Fog is liquid dispersed in a gas.
Opal is a solid dispersed in a solid, not a liquid-in-solid solution.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Chlorine does not have one valence-shell electron.
Chlorine does not have six valence-shell electrons.
Chlorine has seven electrons in its valence shell.
Chlorine has seven, not eight, electrons in its valence shell.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer, not donation of a shared pair.
An ordinary covalent bond forms by sharing, with each atom contributing an electron.
Metallic bonding involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
A coordinate covalent bond forms when one bonded atom supplies both electrons in the shared pair.
Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period.
Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
Electron affinity generally becomes greater across a period, with some exceptions.
Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period.
The L shell can hold more than 6 electrons.
The L shell has a maximum capacity of 8 electrons.
Fourteen is not the maximum capacity of the L shell.
Eighteen is not the maximum capacity of the L shell.
Benzene’s molecular formula C₆H₆ reduces to the empirical formula CH.
C₂H₂ is not the simplest whole-number ratio for benzene.
HO is not the empirical formula of benzene.
CH₂O is not the empirical formula of benzene.
Group 1 and group 2 elements have their valence electrons in the s subshell, so they are s-block elements.
The p block consists of elements whose differentiating electron enters a p subshell.
The d block consists mainly of transition elements.
The f block consists of inner-transition elements.
Liquids are generally denser than gases by much more than 10 times.
A 100-fold difference is generally too small for the comparison intended here.
Liquids are commonly taken to be about 1000 times denser than gases.
A 10000-fold difference is generally too large for the comparison intended here.
% m/m is grams of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% m/v is grams of solute per 100 millilitres of solution.
% v/m is millilitres of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% v/v is millilitres of solute per 100 millilitres of solution.
